question.problem: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{4}{x}$ at the point $(1,4)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $p+q.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{4}{x}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{-1}) \\  & =-4{x}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(1)=-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line ${m}^{′}$ is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(4) & =\frac{1}{4}(x-(1)) \\ 4y-16 & =x-1 \\ x-4y & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p+q=-4+(-15)=-19.$
